The cathedral of Rome, and the church of the pope as bishop of Rome, which ranks it above every other Catholic church, St Peter's included. After Constantine defeated Maxentius at the Milvian Bridge in 312, he pulled down the fort of the imperial horse guard that had fought against him and gave the bishop of Rome the palace next to it, once the house of the Laterani family. Pope Sylvester I dedicated the church to Christ the Saviour in 324, making it the oldest public church in the city; John the Baptist and John the Evangelist were added as patrons in the Middle Ages and gave it its common name. The popes lived in the Lateran Palace until they moved to Avignon in 1309, and five church councils met there, among them the Fourth Lateran Council.

Little of Constantine's building is left. The Vandals stripped its treasures, an earthquake in 897 brought it down "from the altar to the doors", and two fires in the 14th century, in 1308 and in the 1360s, left it badly damaged. Pope Sixtus V had Domenico Fontana build a new palace, and in 1588 raised in the square the Lateran Obelisk, the largest standing ancient Egyptian obelisk, cut for Thutmose III at Karnak and brought to Rome in 357 for the Circus Maximus. For the Jubilee of 1650 Francesco Borromini remade the nave with twelve great niches, filled in 1718 with statues of the apostles. The central doors are the ancient bronze doors of the Senate house in the Roman Forum, moved here under Pope Alexander VII. Alessandro Galilei won a competition for the present facade, finished in 1735.

Beside the church stands the Lateran Baptistery, built by Pope Sixtus III about 440, perhaps on an older building. Legend said Constantine was baptised here; he was more likely baptised in the East. Its octagon, with eight porphyry columns around a large basin for full immersion, was for generations the only baptistery in Rome and a model for many in Italy. It was restored for Pope Urban VIII to plans by Bernini around 1633, with frescoes of the life of Constantine by Andrea Sacchi. Under the Lateran Treaty of 1929 the church and its buildings belong to the Holy See, outside Italian control.
